title: Add service-scoped KMS guardrails and audit ingestion harmonizer
author: Maya Patel
commits: a1b2c3d: introduce service-scoped KMS enforcement middleware and policy API
d4e5f6a: add audit-ingestor that normalizes audit events and attaches residency tags
b7c8d9e: migration: backfill service_kms_id and residency_claim into historical events
f0a1b2c: tests and e2e harness for KMS guardrail and audit ingestion flow
description:
Motivation: Customers operating multiple logical services under the same tenant require strict guarantees that service-A cannot request or unwrap keys bound to service-B. Incidents surfaced during an internal postmortem showed ambiguous key attribution for cross-service operator actions which complicates audits and violates customer isolation promises. This PR implements service-scoped KMS guardrails and a lightweight audit ingestion harmonizer to make audit events canonical and to prevent cross-service key usage by default.

What this PR does (high level): Adds a new enforcement middleware (kms/service-guard) that validates the requesting principal's service claim against the requested key's service binding. Introduces a new policy API to bind keys to a service identifier and to define an exception allowlist for operator flows. Adds an audit-ingestor microservice that normalizes incoming audit records, deduplicates identical events within a short window, enriches events with residency and key binding metadata, and forwards to the existing audit pipeline. Provides a backfill migration to tag historical events with best-effort service_kms_id and residency_claim (logged separately for traceability).

Design notes: - Service binding model: keys have an optional service_id tag set at creation time. When present, only principals with matching service_id or explicit allowlist entries may perform wrap/unwrap or key usage actions. The enforcement is opt-in for existing keys (to avoid breaking legacy customers); new keys have binding encouraged by CLI/console UX. - Failure modes: requests that violate binding fail early with 403 and an structured error code kms.service_bound. Operator-level exceptions can be granted via RBAC role "kms:service-bypass" which requires multi-approver escalation (see RBAC section). - Audit harmonization: the ingestor normalizes heterogenous audit sources (gateway, kms-proxy, operator-proxy) into a canonical event schema (timestamp, principal, service_id, kms_key_id, op, residency_claim, request_id, provenance_chain). It also deduplicates retry storms within a 30s window to reduce noise in retention stores. - Backward compatibility: enforcement for existing keys is behind a feature flag enforcement.kms.service_bind and rollout uses a canary cohort. The ingestor will accept both legacy and canonical payloads and will write a normalized event alongside the original raw event for troubleshooting.

Changed areas (representative): - core/kms/middleware/service_guard.go: new enforcement middleware and policy evaluator - api/kms/policy.go: API surface to bind keys and query service bindings - services/audit/ingestor/*: new service that normalizes, dedupes, enriches audit events and forwards to kafka/topic audit.normalized - infra/eks/manifests/audit-ingestor.yaml: k8s manifest and RBAC for the ingestor - tools/migrations/20241112_backfill_service_kms_tags.go: migration to tag historical events - docs/security/kms-service-binding.md: runbook and operator guidance - tests/e2e/kms_service_binding_test.go and unit tests across middleware/ingestor

Testing and verification: - Unit tests cover policy evaluation matrix, denial messages, and the fallback path for unbound keys. - Integration tests run a mini-ingestor and replayed audit payloads validating normalization and dedupe behavior. - E2E smoke includes creation of bound key, attempt to use key with non-matching service principal (expect 403), and operator unbind flow (requires role and audit note). - CI: lint, unit, integration, and e2e stages passed on the merge run (flaky test t-queue-429 retried once).

Migration and rollout plan: - Phase 1 (canary): enable audit-ingestor in staging and wire a 5% subset of production traffic for 48h. Run backfill in read-only mode to evaluate heuristics. - Phase 2 (soft enforcement): enable service_bind enforcement for newly-created keys and opt-in existing keys via console prompts. Run with monitoring dashboards for reject rate and false positives. - Phase 3 (enforce for cohort): enable enforcement for a subset of tenants that opted-in; continue backfill and provide operator tooling to request exception. - Phase 4 (global): flip enforcement.kms.service_bind and promote ingestor as primary audit-normalizer.

Rollout guards and SLOs: - Alert if reject rate for bound-key usage > 0.1% of normal traffic for 1h and if normalized audit ingest latency > 500ms p95. - Provide a rollback flag to disable enforcement cluster-wide within 15 minutes.

Security and compliance notes: - Audit events now include canonical residency_claim and service_kms_id; these fields are surfaced to Compliance exports. - RBAC: introduced new role kms:service-bypass that is gated by two approvers for granting via the console; role change events are captured by the ingestor. - KMS provider compatibility: enforcement checks are performed in the request flow and do not require KMS provider changes (we attach binding metadata at Redwood's metadata layer).

Related work and references: Linear ENG-8842 (design doc), SEC-1471 compliance review. Follow-ups: integrate key binding UI in Console (tracked in ENG-9129) and rotation flow to preserve bindings (ENG-9204).

Files changed summary: small code additions across middleware and a new service. No schema changes to core tenant records; audit store schema extended with optional fields (backfill added separately). Storage impact estimated ~1.2% increase in retention store per event due to added metadata.

Merge: squash and merge. This PR includes migration scripts and an operator playbook under docs.
review_comments: Elliot Zhang: Can we ensure the middleware runs before any request body parsing to avoid accidental caching of malformed requests? Also suggest a clear error code for automation consumers.
Maya Patel (author): Reordered middleware chain so service_guard is executed immediately after auth. Added structured error code 'kms.service_bound' and included error docs link in response.
Ravi Desai: Approving after requested tests added. Logged a follow-up for console UX (ENG-9129).
release_notes: Add service-scoped KMS guardrails to prevent cross-service key access and introduce an audit-ingestor that normalizes and deduplicates audit events. Backfill migration provided. Feature gated and rolled out in controlled cohorts.
